subject: Commit tenor & phased onramp alignment — Veridian AI
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Commit tenor & phased onramp alignment — Veridian AI

Hi Amy — thanks for the productive demo earlier this week. Per our conversation I put together three practical commit tenors and a suggested phased onramp we can use as the starting point for commercial discussion. Key points below; attached is a one-page pricing schedule and our Dedicated technical spec for the proposed GPU pool.

Summary (high-level):
- Term options: 12 / 24 / 36 months.
- Baseline pool sizing (example): 40x A100 equivalent GPUs for initial capacity, bursting to +60% during business hours via reserved burst pool.
- Throughput SLAs: target sustained throughput 420k tokens/min for the baseline pool; guaranteed 95th%-ile token generation latency <= 250ms for p95 prompts under the baseline profile.
- Discount bands (illustrative): 12mo = 10% off list, 24mo = 18%, 36mo = 24%. Volume breakout and exact $/vGPU/month in attached CSV.
- Ramp schedule: 3-phase onramp over 3 months (Month 0: pilot capacity ~30% of baseline, Month 1: 60% baseline, Month 2+: full baseline). Start date is flexible — we can push to June 1 or target earlier May 15 start if underwriting completes.

Open asks for Veridian:
1) Confirm preferred term (12/24/36) and whether you need a mid-term scale-up option.
2) Share a 6-month MAU/throughput forecast (attached works) so we can size the burst pool and confirm q-guardrails.
3) Any procurement/legal constraints (PO timing, signature authority) and SOC2 evidence needs.

Next steps: Marcus / Karthik — any sizing or SLA tweaks before I send a more formal commercial worksheet? Amy — if this looks good I can push a draft commercial term sheet + DocuSign link by Friday.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0147

Attachments: Proposed_Pricing_Schedule.csv, Redwood_Dedicated_Technical_Specs.pdf
From: Amy Chen <amy@veridian.ai>

Cc: sales_ops@veridian.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit tenor & phased onramp alignment — Veridian AI

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- We like the 24mo as the default target but would consider 12mo if you can add a 6-week trial credit window and stronger ramp protection (i.e., ability to step up without penalty in month 6).
- Can you show a worked example for $/vGPU/month and effective $/M tokens for the 24mo band? The CSV is helpful but a line-item example would make it easier for procurement.
- SOC2 and data residency: we need SOC2 Type II report and confirmation that logs/audit trails are retained for 12 months.

I attached a short 6-month MAU forecast and a note on our procurement timeline (we need signed terms by end of May to hit Q3 roadmap gating).

If you can get a revised sheet with a line-item example + DocuSign by next Tue (Apr 7) I’ll circulate internally.

—Amy

Subject: Re: Commit tenor & phased onramp alignment — Veridian AI

On Fri, Apr 3, 2026 at 9:14 AM Amy Chen <amy@veridian.ai> wrote:
> Can you show a worked example for $/vGPU/month and effective $/M tokens for the 24mo band?

Hi Amy — quick sizing/throughput notes from infra that will feed the worked pricing example:
- The MAU spike profile you shared maps to a steady-state inference throughput of ~480k tokens/min with 80 concurrent streams (avg prompt seq len ~220).
- For that shape we'd recommend an initial pool of 48 A100-equivalent slots with a 30-slot burst reserve (burst is warmed and pre-reserved for predictable latency).
- With continuous batching and KV caching we estimate effective cost-per-1000-tokens to be ~45% lower than naive per-token pricing; I’ll show the math in the worksheet.
- Latency guarantees: p95 <= 250ms for prompts under 512 tokens if the burst pool is available. If burst is exhausted latency SLO falls back to p95 <= 450ms until burst replenishes.

I’ll model two scenarios in the worked example: (A) 24mo steady-state (48 baseline, 30 burst), (B) conservative 24mo (40 baseline, 20 burst) so you can choose trade-offs.

-Karthik
Principal Solution Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy@veridian.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit tenor & phased onramp alignment — Veridian AI

Amy / team — building on Karthik’s notes, here’s a commercial tweak we can offer to align risk and timeline. Numbers below are for discussion — final $/vGPU in attached CSV but I pulled the effective math into bullets: 

Offer (workshop-level):
- 12mo: 10% off list, onboarding credit = $30k one-time; standard 3-mo ramp (pilot month at 30%).
- 24mo: 18% off list, onboarding credit = $75k (covers migration + priority engineering support), 3-phase ramp but with optional mid-term scale-up at month 6 without penalty (one-time true-up).
- 36mo: 24% off list, onboarding credit = $125k, includes 6 months of discounted burst capacity at 50% extra for free during year 1.

Other commercial notes:
- To secure the 24mo rate we need executed terms by May 20 (pricing protected until EOD May 20).
- We can include a 6-week pilot credit for the 24mo offer if Veridian signs a non-binding letter of intent this week — credit applied against month 1 invoice.
- SLA & audit: SOC2 Type II evidence will be made available to your security team once we sign an NDA / DPA; long-term log retention is configurable and we can commit to 12-month retention for the Dedicated deployment.

If 24mo looks like the right path I can generate a redline-ready term sheet and DocuSign envelope for signature — target signature date May 18 to avoid billing cycle edge cases.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — this is close to what we need. Veridian prefers the 24mo with the $75k onboarding credit and the month-6 scale-up flexibility. Two requests before procurement will greenlight:
1) Please provide a line-item worked example showing effective $/M tokens for our forecasted Month 3 and Month 9 volumes (you mentioned you’d model that).
2) We need SOC2 Type II and a draft DPA redline; legal will only sign after SOC2 is validated.

We’re aiming to start capacity on June 1 and close commercial terms by May 18. I’ll loop in procurement if you share the DocuSign link and the redline-ready term sheet.

—Amy
